questions.q: What are the four stages of a Variational Quantum Classifier pipeline, in order?
options: Encode classical data, apply the trainable ansatz, measure an observable, convert to prediction and compute loss then update parameters
Measure, encode, update parameters, apply ansatz
Apply ansatz, encode, compute loss, measure
Only two stages: encode and measure, with no training loop
questions.explain: The VQC pipeline assembles encoding (Lesson 10), the trainable ansatz (Lesson 6), measurement (Lesson 5), and the loss/parameter-shift/optimizer update loop (Lessons 2 and 7) into one complete pipeline.

questions.q: If a trained circuit outputs <Z> = 0.6, what is the predicted probability p using p = (<Z>+1)/2, and what class is predicted at threshold p >= 0.5?
options: p = 0.8, predicted class 1
p = 0.6, predicted class 0
p = 0.3, predicted class 0
p = 1.6, predicted class 1
questions.explain: p = (0.6+1)/2 = 0.8, which is above the 0.5 threshold, so the sample is predicted class 1 with 80% confidence.

questions.q: For true label y=1 and predicted probability p=0.8, what is the binary cross-entropy loss L = -[y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)]?
options: Approximately 0.2231
Approximately 0.9163
Exactly 0
Approximately 0.8000
questions.explain: Since y=1, the loss reduces to -log(0.8), which is approximately 0.2231 -- a small but nonzero loss, since cross-entropy only reaches exactly 0 at p=1.0 for a true-label-1 sample.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a confidently wrong-leaning prediction (p=0.4 for true label y=1) produces a loss over 4 times larger than a confidently correct one (p=0.8 for the same true label)?
options: -log(0.4) is approximately 0.9163 versus -log(0.8) approximately 0.2231 -- cross-entropy penalizes confident wrong predictions much more heavily than confident correct ones
Binary cross-entropy loss is always exactly proportional to (1-p) regardless of the actual probability value
The loss function used here is actually squared error, not cross-entropy
There is no real difference; both losses are approximately equal
questions.explain: The logarithm in cross-entropy grows steeply as p moves away from the true label's side, which is exactly why -log(0.4) (about 0.9163) is more than 4x larger than -log(0.8) (about 0.2231) for the same true label.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say 'I built a VQC' is the start of a technical conversation rather than the end of one?
options: Because a VQC is a template with several independent design choices (encoding, ansatz structure, observable, optimizer), each a research question with no universally correct answer
Because VQCs are purely theoretical and none can actually be built or run
Because every VQC implementation is mathematically identical regardless of design choices
Because only Qiskit's prebuilt VQC class counts as a real VQC
questions.explain: The specific encoding, ansatz depth/structure, observable choice, and optimizer all significantly affect training behavior and results, so naming the architecture alone says little about how well it will actually perform.
